evidence.quote: We should encourage our children to do what they like

claims.adjudication_reason: Second-review support: In turn 1, A addresses B's anger toward specific children ('Don't be angry with them. After all, they are still children.'). In turn 3, A refers to those same children as 'our children.' The definite possessive 'our children' in direct address to B presupposes that B has children — even under an inclusive 'we' reading (e.g., 'we as parents'), the presupposition that B is a parent of these children remains. Rejecting this would require assuming a non-parental relationship (teacher, community member) which is not supported by the text and would be speculation against the most natural reading.
